Apply PHW styling to a plotly chart

Source: R/html-widgets.R
phw_plotly.Rd

Restyles a plotly figure with the PHW font, colour order, light gridlines, a horizontal legend under the chart, and hover labels in navy. It also trims the mode bar. You can pass it a plotly object, or a ggplot, which is converted with plotly::ggplotly() first.

Usage

phw_plotly(
  p,
  source = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  ...,
  legend = c("bottom", "right", "none"),
  palette = phw_default_palette(),
  font_size = 13,
  caption_args = list(),
  modebar = TRUE
)

Arguments

p

A plotly object or a ggplot.

source, date

Passed to phw_caption() and shown under the chart.

...

Extra arguments for plotly::layout(). They override the PHW defaults; lists are merged, so title = list(text = "My title") keeps the PHW title style.

legend

"bottom", "right" or "none".

palette

Colour order for traces that don't set their own colour: a palette name or a vector of colours.

font_size

Base font size in px.

caption_args

List of other phw_caption() arguments.

modebar

Show the plotly tool bar?

Value

A plotly object.

Details

Any plotly chart type works: scatter and lines, bars, pies and donuts (given the PHW colours and white slice borders), box and violin plots, histograms, heatmaps and choropleth maps (which pick up the PHW sequential colour scale unless you set colorscale), and figures combined with plotly::subplot(). Use phw_plotly_colorscale() to set a PHW scale on a trace yourself.

For colours that stay with a group across charts, pass a colour key to plotly yourself, e.g. plot_ly(df, x = ~week, y = ~rate, color = ~age, colors = phw_colour_key(df$age, "age")). ggplots keep the colours of their scale_colour_phw_d(key = ...).

Examples

if (requireNamespace("plotly", quietly = TRUE)) {
  df <- data.frame(week = rep(1:10, 2),
                   cases = c(3, 5, 9, 14, 20, 18, 13, 9, 6, 4,
                             2, 4, 6, 9, 11, 13, 12, 10, 7, 5),
                   group = rep(c("Group A", "Group B"), each = 10))

  # A chart built with plot_ly()
  p <- plotly::plot_ly(df, x = ~week, y = ~cases, color = ~group,
                       type = "scatter", mode = "lines")
  w1 <- phw_plotly(p, source = "Example data")

  # A ggplot, converted for you
  g <- ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(week, cases, colour = group)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line()
  w2 <- phw_plotly(g, source = "Example data", hovermode = "x")

  # Printing shows the chart in the Viewer or a browser.
  if (interactive()) print(w1)
}
